⭐ The Golden Rule: read this first

There is no official per-role stat list in Aniimo. What the game itself gives you is per-Aniimo: every Aniimo's panel marks two Recommended Attributes, in priority order (1st and 2nd), plus thumbs-up marks on the stats its skills actually scale from.

So the role tables in this guide are the best general baselines the guide community has, but always trust your Aniimo's own Recommended Attributes and thumbs-ups over its role label. AniimoEggs · AniimoTools · AllThings How

⚔️ Stats, Roles & Elements

Six stats, five roles, no Tank badge. Here's what each stat really does, what each role really wants, and the two places where the popular advice is just plain wrong.

✨ The Six Stats

❤️
HP

Health and survivability. For healers it's double-duty: heals are a share of the healer's own Max HP, so HP is also healing power.

🗡️
ATK

Damage output, but not for everyone. Four of the five roles barely touch ATK for their basic hits (see the formulas below).

💥
BREAK

Drains the enemy's guard / break gauge to create openings. For DPS and Breakers it can also be their damage stat, at 85% strength.

🛡️
P.DEF

Physical resistance. Covers physical damage only, that's why leftover points usually go to HP instead, which guards against everything.

🔮
M.DEF

Magic resistance. Like P.DEF, it covers one damage type only, pick the defense that matches the fight you're heading into.

🔋
REGEN

"Increases Energy recovery speed to cast skills faster" (in-game tooltip). It's EP regen for skill uptime, not HP regeneration and not Speed. Only the on-field Aniimo's REGEN feeds the shared party Energy pool.

Stat definitions agree across TheGamesWiki, AniimoVerse, and AniimoTools. One caveat (AniimoVerse, single source): client data also stores a separate hidden Magic Attack that differs from ATK on a minority of forms, so ATK isn't always the whole story for Magic skills.

🎯 The Five Roles: Stats in Order of Importance

🔥 DPS

Damage Dealer
Top statsATK → REGEN*

Full order: 1 ATK · 2 REGEN · 3 BREAK · 4 HP · 5–6 P.DEF / M.DEF (take the one matching the fight). REGEN holds #2 on flagship panels; BREAK is the situational pick, it speeds up gauge drain but never adds damage.

  • ATK #1 is unanimous: every source agrees.
  • The old claim "ATK then BREAK" is oversimplified: the game's own Recommended Attributes for flagship DPS Lunara, Ignitis and Fulmintis are ATK + REGEN.
  • BREAK Potential still has a use (it drains the enemy gauge faster), but for a DPS it never adds HP damage.

AniimoTools damage formula · AniimoVerse · AllThings builds

💥 BREAK

Guard Breaker
Top statsBREAK → HP / P.DEF

Full order: 1 BREAK · 2 HP · 3–4 P.DEF / M.DEF (match the fight) · 5 REGEN · 6 ATK, dead last: 25 of 26 Breakers never use it, so skip it.

  • BREAK #1: it's both gauge damage and, at 0.85×, their HP damage.
  • The old claim "BREAK then ATK" is refuted: 25 of 26 Breakers never use their ATK at all. Popota is the lone exception.
  • Frontline order: BREAK → HP → the defense matching the fight → REGEN.

AniimoTools damage formula · AllThings builds · AniimoVerse

🎵 SUPPORT

Buffer & Control
Top statsDepends on the kit!

Baseline order: 1 REGEN · 2 HP · 3–4 P.DEF / M.DEF · then ATK or BREAK only if this Aniimo's skills scale with them (15 Support/REGEN skills scale with ATK, 6 with REGEN). The kit always outranks this list.

  • REGEN + HP is a plausible baseline, not a law, Support is the role where the Golden Rule matters most.
  • Skill scaling splits: 15 Support/REGEN skills grow with ATK (cap 800 ATK, up to ×1.4); 6 grow with REGEN (cap 500).
  • Named ATK-scaling exceptions: Tromber, Luminelle, Eklue.

AniimoTools damage formula · AllThings · AniimoVerse · MetaBot.GG

⚡ REGEN

Energy Provider
Top statsREGEN → HP

Full order: 1 REGEN · 2 HP · 3–4 P.DEF / M.DEF · 5 ATK · 6 BREAK, basic attacks for this role effectively ignore ATK, and BREAK never counts at all.

  • REGEN #1 is unanimous: the best-supported #2 pairing of any role. REGEN-role Aniimo carry the roster's highest average REGEN (106.2).
  • The signature skills of Leafy, Besauce, Somniwing, Erlath and Flamerion grow with REGEN, up to a 500 cap.
  • A few REGEN Aniimo (Hexxin, Fragrancier, Leafy, Somniwing) list REGEN as their only priority, HP is the usual runner-up, not a guarantee.

AniimoVerse · AniimoTools · MetaBot.GG · AllThings builds

💗 HEAL

Healer, the rarest role
Top statsHP → REGEN

Full order: 1 HP · 2 REGEN · 3–4 P.DEF / M.DEF · 5 ATK · 6 BREAK, BREAK is the lowest priority for a healer; usually skip it entirely.

  • HP #1 verified: heals are a set share of the healer's own Max HP, so Max HP is both survivability and heal size.
  • REGEN is co-#2 at best: even the order flips per Aniimo, the flagship Gracewing's build lists "Regen, HP", while Prismana Glacy is HP only.
  • The whole playable roster is five: Skippy, Pranky, Glacy, Flutternym, Gracewing, all Water or Wind. Bubbeep and Glameep exist in the game data but are unreleased.

AniimoTools · MetaBot.GG · AniimoGuide healer list · AllThings builds

💥 How Damage Actually Works

Basic attacks: DPS & BREAK roles verified ×2 sources

Basic attack power = max( ATK , 0.85 × BREAK )

A DPS or Breaker hits with whichever is higher. This is exactly why ATK is dead weight on most Breakers: 25 of 26 hit with their BREAK side of the formula. One tested Breaker (Blazen) at 510 ATK vs 0.85 × 770 BREAK = 654 was swinging entirely on BREAK, its ATK points did nothing.

Measured in-game by AniimoTools; independently stated by AllThings How.

Basic attacks: Support, REGEN & Heal roles disputed: floor vs flat

Basic attack power = max( ATK , 10.5 × level )

One source (AllThings) says these roles ignore ATK completely and hit for a flat 10.5 × level (~640 at Lv 60). AniimoTools (equally recent, more detailed, and claiming developer confirmation in October 2026) says it's a floor: ATK counts, but only once it climbs above 10.5 × level, and BREAK never counts. The floor reading is better supported, but the disagreement isn't fully closed. The practical takeaway both sides agree on: for a typical Support/REGEN/Heal, ATK investment does nothing for basic attacks, and BREAK never does.

Healing verified

Heal size = a set % of the healer's own Max HP, no ceiling

Gracewing heals the whole team for 30% of its Max HP at once, plus 9% over 8 seconds. Glacy's Healing Water restores 10% of the caster's Max HP to all allies. Caveat: this is verified for Heal-role kits, the skill text always rules, and some healing effects elsewhere are written off the recipient's HP or as a fixed percentage instead.

AniimoTools · Hideout (Glacy) · AniimoVerse

🌍 Elements: what the verified research does (and doesn't) cover

Elements run through the whole game, every playable healer is Water or Wind (§1, Heal card), homeland facilities ask for element-tied Home Abilities, and a whole band of element-affinity traits grants flat bonuses in three tiers (HP, damage, damage reduction and Crit Rate at +5/10/15%; Crit Damage at +7.5/15/22.5%, full table in §4). What the verified research does not contain is an official element matchup chart: the "~1.6× damage when advantaged, ~0.625× when resisted" numbers circulating in fan drafts are single-source and unverified, so they're kept in the §4 quarantine box instead of printed here as fact. When a cross-checked matchup chart exists, it will live in this spot.

🎭 All Eight Personality Traits

Every Aniimo rolls one trait from each pair (E/I · S/N · T/F · J/P), making its 4-letter personality. All four combat bonuses stack together, and each trait also boosts specific homeland facilities. These bonuses do double duty: they shape both your battles and your homeland staffing.

✅ Verified: four sources, digit for digit

GameWith, Game8, AniimoTools and Selphie1999 Gaming all reproduce the game's own in-game Combat Bonus / Home Bonus panels with identical values, this is the most solidly confirmed table in the whole guide. (One outlier site, DTGRE, prints different names and values for E, I and N, against four sources showing the actual in-game panels, those values are disregarded. If you see "Clingy" or Crit Rate +3% anywhere, that's the bad table.)

🚫 Myth-bust: there are NO personality "strength" grades

You may see guides claiming traits come in Somewhat +3% / Relatively +6% / Very +10% strengths. That ladder does exist in the game's data files, but AniimoTools, which found it there, states flatly that it does nothing: the entries have no effect attached, and no Aniimo can ever be given one. It's datamined dead data, not a live system. One database (Hideout) prints it as if it were live on every character page, that's where the claim spreads from. In the real game, every letter is worth one fixed bonus, full stop.

AniimoTools, Potential Score & Traits

🍑 Changing Personality: the Psyche Fruit

How it works

  • Feed an Aniimo a Psyche Fruit and all four letters reroll at random, you can't choose the result, so landing a target code can take several fruit.
  • No limit on uses, keep rerolling the same Aniimo until you get the stats you want. Budget for several attempts.
  • It changes only personality, not Home Abilities, level, skills, Potential or rarity.
  • Personality otherwise never changes: it's rolled when the Aniimo is obtained/hatched, and levels and evolution don't touch it.
  • One more reason to reroll: certain evolution stages require specific personality traits, an Aniimo with the wrong personality can be stuck until you change it. (AniimoEggs)

Cost & warnings

  • 100 Glimmer per fruit in the shop, no purchase limit shown. (Game8 shop guide · AllThings · Nerdschalk: three sources agree)
  • Also earnable without the shop, via Elite Training missions, the Item Exchange and the Companion Handbook. (AllThings)
  • ⚠️ The change happens immediately, with no confirmation pop-up, double-check which Aniimo is selected before feeding. (Game8)
  • 🔒 Locked starters: Helion (ENFP) and Lunara (ISTJ) can never change personality, the game returns a "cannot change personalities" error. (Game8 · AniimoTools)
  • single source A daily Mysterious Vendor reportedly sells 3 Psyche Fruit per day for 420,000 Credits total, reported by Nerdschalk only, not yet corroborated.

🏆 Personality Recommendations by Combat Role

Five guide sources, and they agree on almost everything, E-first for damage, I-first for sustain, and one baseline code that shows up everywhere. The single real fight is over Breakers, and it's presented honestly below.

🔥 DPS
ESTJ
Crit kit → ENTJ

ATK, flat damage, and a sturdy T/J defensive pairing. E-first for DPS is unanimous across all five sources.

💥 BREAK
ISTP
Crit kit → INTP · ⚔️ debated, see below

GameWith's pick: give up the attack bonus for REGEN, so break skills keep casting. The majority of guides pick the E family instead.

🎵 SUPPORT
ISTJ
Crit kit → INTJ

REGEN for skill uptime, HP for staying on the field. Per-Aniimo builds split by kit, ATK-scaling Supports are the exception class.

⚡ REGEN
ISTJ
The energy battery build

Same baseline as Support and Heal. Two guide sources don't even separate REGEN out, they fold it into the sustain group, and still land here.

💗 HEAL
ISTJ
REGEN +4% · HP +4%

Faster heal cycles, bigger Max HP pool, and since heals scale off Max HP, J's HP +4% is quietly also a healing bonus.

Baselines from GameWith (updated 21 Oct 2026, the most recent personality guide found, and the only one that argues its picks from game mechanics). ISTJ for Heal/Support is additionally named by Game8 and Selphie1999, and AllThings' per-Aniimo builds land on ISTJ for Gracewing, Prismana Glacy, and most REGEN-role Aniimo, making ISTJ the single best-supported personality recommendation in the game.

🎯 The crit rule: S by default, N only for crit kits

GameWith's rule, echoed independently by Selphie1999, DTGRE and AllThings' crit builds: start with S (flat DMG +4%). If the word "crit" appears anywhere in the Aniimo's skills or its trait, swap S for N (Crit Rate +5%). The reasoning: Crit Rate is worth nothing on an Aniimo with no way to use crits, so flat damage wins by default. Game8 is the lone outlier, prescribing N for all DPS regardless of kit, the crit-conditional view is better supported, four sources to one.

⚔️ The Great Breaker Debate: ESTJ/ESTP vs ISTP/INTP

This is the one genuinely unresolved question in Aniimo character building. Nobody on either side has published head-to-head testing, no casts-per-fight, time-to-break, or clear-time comparisons exist anywhere as of 23 Oct 2026. Here's both cases, fairly:

Team E: ESTJ / ESTP family 4 sources

Who: Game8 (ESTP/ESFP/ESTJ/ESFJ), Selphie1999 (all E-codes for BREAK), DTGRE (E as the first Break trait), and AllThings' per-Aniimo builds (E-codes for every Breaker listed).

The argument: simple stat-matching. E is the only letter that raises BREAK at all (+2%), and it throws in ATK +2% besides. If you want more break, take the letter that says break on it.

Team I: ISTP / INTP 1 source, but the newest

Who: GameWith alone (personality guide updated 21 Oct 2026, the most recent found).

The argument: a Breaker's job is done by skills: Break Power moves against the gauge, skills cost EP, and REGEN is what refills EP. So +4% REGEN buys more break-skill casts. Meanwhile E's bonus is half wasted: the verified damage formula (§1) shows a Breaker's damage comes from 0.85 × BREAK, not ATK, so on 25 of 26 Breakers, E's ATK +2% half does literally nothing, and E effectively offers only BREAK +2% against I's full REGEN +4%.

⚖️ The honest verdict

Unresolved, with an evidence-weighted edge to GameWith. On headcount, E wins 4–1. On mechanism, GameWith's reasoning is corroborated by two independently verified facts (the 0.85 × BREAK formula, and gauge damage being driven by the BREAK stat plus the equipped move's Break Power, i.e. by casting repeatedly, exactly what REGEN feeds), and the E-side guides never address either. GameWith is also the most recently updated source, and its picks come from stated rules that reproduce the consensus picks for every other role.

The practical stakes are small either way: the whole fight is over BREAK +2% versus REGEN +4% on a single letter. If you want one pick: ISTP (INTP for a crit-kit Breaker) is the better-argued choice; ESTJ/ESTP is the majority-consensus choice. Neither is wrong enough to waste Psyche Fruit chasing the other.

One careful addition on crits (checked 28 Oct 2026): critical hits can add break damage on some Break Aniimo, Game8's build for Beach Tubster picks Nimble (Crit Rate +5%) for exactly this, so crit is kit-dependent for Breakers, not a blanket priority. It changes nothing about the stat order in §1: Attack stays last for the role either way.

💎 Potentials, Held Items & Upgrades

Every Aniimo carries a hidden quality grade and a Potential value for each of its six stats. This section separates what's verified (AniimoTools' system pages and AniimoEggs, both working from the game itself) from numbers still circulating unverified, they're quarantined in the box at the bottom, not mixed into the facts.

⭐ The Potential Score: your Aniimo's hidden grade

Sort or filter your Collection by Potential Score and each Aniimo shows one of four ascending quality grades. The grade isn't an average: the game adds up Innate Potential with the species' two Recommended Attributes counted three times: 3 × (the two recommended) + the other four.

GradeWild catch oddsWeighted total neededPlain total, at least
Common66%n/an/a
Good26%3216
Elite7.2%4824
Perfect0.8%6432

The natural maximum is a weighted 80 (plain 40). The 20 Prismana forms roll a kinder table and are never Common: 80% Good, 18.6% Elite, 1.4% Perfect. Rarer catch sources and certain areas ("you are more likely to catch high-potential Aniimo in this area") shift the roll upward. AniimoTools, Potential Score & Traits

🌱 Innate + Acquired: how Potential grows

🌱 Innate Potential: rolled at capture

  • 0 to 10 on each stat, set when you obtain the Aniimo. Innate alone never goes past 10 on a stat.
  • Only two things raise it afterwards: a Capafruit (+1 Innate to all six stats, once per Aniimo) and some events (+1 to one attribute, up to 4 times, the game counts them: "Innate Potential has been additionally upgraded 1/4 times").
  • Best use of a Capafruit: save it for an Aniimo whose two Recommended Attributes both sit at Innate 9. The fruit's +1 to all six stats crowns both at 10 at once, earning the Perfect badge its sunglasses (see the legend below). Spent on anything lower, the same fruit buys points you could have awakened more cheaply. (Checked 28 Oct 2026: AllThings Capability Awakening guide · Game8 · GameWith · AniimoTools)
  • AniimoTools puts the most Innate Potential any Aniimo can hold at 48 in total.

✨ Acquired Potential: Capability Awakening

  • On the Awaken tab, pick a stat and spend awakening materials to raise that stat's Acquired Potential by one point. The game's own rule: "In the Capability Awakening system, you can consume Star Dust and other items to increase an Aniimo's Acquired Potential for the selected attribute." Those "other items" are Star Sand and Starcryst Essence: one stat climbs all three materials in order (full ladder in the box below).
  • Each point adds +0.8% of the stat and +6 CP, and every 4 points add another +4%. A stat pushed to 20/20 is about +39% stronger than at 0.
  • Spend on the thumbs-up stats first (§7, and the legend below), they're the ones the Aniimo's skills scale from.

Capability Awakening: the full materials ladder checked 28 Oct 2026

Awakening one stat climbs three materials in order. The early steps are cheap; the back half is where the rare material lives:

  • Steps 1–4 · Star Dust: ×1, ×2, ×3, ×4 (10 in total).
  • Steps 5–8 · Star Sand: ×1, ×2, ×3, ×4 (10 in total).
  • Steps 9–20 · Starcryst Essence: ×1, ×2, then ×3 and ×4 at steps 11–12, then ×5 each from step 13 on (50 in total).
  • Total per stat, all the way to 20: 10 Star Dust · 10 Star Sand · 50 Starcryst Essence.
  • Level gates on the way up: steps 11–12 need the Aniimo at Lv 40, steps 13–15 need Lv 50, steps 16–19 need Lv 55, and step 20 needs Lv 60.

Starcryst Essence is the bottleneck. Omega Infergon is the only boss that drops it (×2 per fight, 3 fights a week). The other routes: Elite Training quests, the Holo-Battle Sim and Interlink, the Item Exchange (20 Star Sand for 2 Essence), the Glimmer shop, and the Season Stamp Shop. Budget your essence for thumbs-up stats first, exactly because it is this scarce.

Checked 28 Oct 2026 against the AllThings Capability Awakening guide, Game8, GameWith, AniimoTools and Daily Aniimo.

The cap, and the ways past it

Innate + Acquired ≤ 20 per stat (the game's "Potential Limit")
  • Two sources describe two different systems for pushing a stat past 20, they may stack, but neither source spells out how they interact, so they're kept separate here: AniimoTools describes Resonance stage-ups at levels 50, 60 and 65 adding +1, +1 and +2 to all six Potentials (4 in all), past the limit.
  • AniimoEggs describes the Resident Star Up tab, which lets favorable (thumbs-up) stats pass the standard cap and reach a maximum Potential of 24.
  • Held items sit on top: they're an equipment slot (called "carried items" in the beta) adding bonuses beyond what Potential alone allows. One verified example, Giant Tortoise Shell: M.DEF Potential +2, P.DEF Potential +2. (AniimoEggs · AniimoTools)
  • Held items, two verified conditions checked 28 Oct 2026: an item's +2 Potential applies once the item reaches enhancement +10, not before; and a Legendary item at Lv 15 unlocks its Tier 2 effect and can form a Contract (cost: 10 Mark of the Strong). (AllThings · Game8 · GameWith · AniimoTools · Daily Aniimo)
  • Myth check: Potential is per-stat, there is no single "Potential 1–5" slider on fan wikis, and it is not locked at capture. Levelling runs on a separate Resonance Training ladder. (AniimoTools)

A separate band of traits grants a flat bonus tied to an Aniimo's element affinity, six kinds, each in three tiers (AniimoTools):

HP

🔣 Symbols & Badges: what the little icons mean

The game marks important things with tiny symbols instead of words. Every entry below is confirmed by AniimoTools (working from the game's own screens and data) or AniimoEggs (re-checked against the released game), nothing here is guessed. The badge colors are shown the way AniimoTools displays the game's quality badges.

Quality grade badges: Common · Good · Elite · Perfect

Each appraised Aniimo wears one of four colored quality badges for its Potential Score: green Common, blue Good, purple Elite, gold Perfect (the Perfect badge even has a happy, sparkly face). Higher badge = higher weighted Innate Potential roll, see the grade table above for odds and thresholds.

❓

"Unappraised"

A freshly caught Aniimo's grade is hidden, its Potential Score reads Unappraised until you appraise it to reveal which of the four badges it earned. An Unappraised Aniimo isn't a bad one; its roll just hasn't been shown yet.

🕶️

The "Sunglass Perfect"

When both of an Aniimo's Recommended Attributes reach 10 Innate Potential, its Perfect grade badge wears sunglasses. It's the game's way of showing a Perfect whose two most important stats are maxed at their natural roll, the rarest version of the rarest grade.

👍

Thumbs-up: Recommended Attributes

On the stats panel and the Capability Awakening (Awaken) screen, the game marks the Aniimo's two Recommended Attributes with a thumbs-up. These are its "favorable" stats, the ones its skills scale from, the ones counted triple in its grade, and the ones that can reach Potential 24 via Star Up. Example: a Perfect Lunara's panel shows Innate 8·4·4·4·8·4 with thumbs-ups on the two 8s, ATK and REGEN. When in doubt, feed the thumbs-ups.

👑

Crown: a maxed stat

A crown icon appears next to a stat once it reaches its maximum attribute limit, players call fully maxing a stat "crowning" it (maxing everything is "double crowning"). Watch the Perfect badge too: a crown on the Perfect icon itself means every individual stat is maxed. A Perfect grade alone does not guarantee that, look for the crown.

EI

Blue pill / pink pill: personality poles

On the personality panels, the game colors the two poles of each axis differently: a blue pill is the first pole (E, S, T, J) and a pink pill is the second (I, N, F, P). Handy when you're scanning a panel quickly for the letters you want.

👀 Spotted in the data: NOT confirmed in the live game

Extrovert Effort, a team-wide trait sitting in the same data table as the personality panels: "Increases ATK by 2% when all Aniimo in your party are [Instinctive] Aniimo." AniimoTools lists it as not confirmed in game yet, so don't build around it. It's here only so the name doesn't confuse you if you meet it in a datamine. (Same drawer as the dead Somewhat/Relatively/Very ladder in §2.)

Legend sources: AniimoTools, Potential Score & Traits · AniimoEggs, Capability Points, Fruits and Crowning Stats (re-checked against the released game 27 Sep 2026) · AllThings, Capability Awakening

🧪 Not yet verified: from a community working draft, do not treat as fact

These numbers are circulating in fan-made drafts and posters, but no source in the verified research confirms them. They're listed so you can recognize them, not so you spend resources based on them yet:

  • Specific held-item effects and numbers (e.g. "Ferocious Fang: Damage Amp +10%, +0.7 ATK per level", "Spirited Feather: REGEN +10%"), and even the total item count: databases disagree on whether there are 24 or 25 held items.
  • Held-item enhancement caps by rarity (Rare +5 / Epic +10 / Legendary +15, with "Advanced Effect" tiers). Two held-item conditions are now verified and live in the box above: the +2 Potential at enhancement +10, and the Legendary Lv 15 Tier 2 effect and Contract.
  • A Potential reset costing 200,000 Gold (with a level-60-or-below restriction and a free first reset).
  • Element matchup multipliers of ~1.6× damage when advantaged and ~0.625× when resisted.
  • Poster claims that Star Up "adds +2 to all six stats and raises the cap to 22". AniimoEggs does verify that favorable stats can reach 24 via Resident Star Up, but the poster's exact mechanics aren't confirmed.

The Kairos - Aniimo upgrade-guide video ("Stop Wasting Resources!") was cross-checked on 28 October 2026: its awakening costs, Capafruit tip and held-item conditions checked out against AllThings, Game8, GameWith, AniimoTools and Daily Aniimo and are folded into this section above. Two of its numbers did not check out and were kept out: a "20% loss" when feeding upgraded items into legendaries appears in no source, and its Counter Boost figure is +20% in AniimoTools' Resonance stage table (T4), not the higher number the video states.

🏡 Homeland Quick Reference

Personality does double duty: the same letters that buff combat also staff your homeland. Match a worker's personality to a facility's listed trait and that Aniimo works +20% more efficiently there, but only while assigned there, and only at its matching facilities. The rate is the same +20% for all eight traits; what changes is which facilities each one favors. (GameWith)

🏡 Staffing checklist

  • Match the letter to the facility, the +20% applies only at the facilities listed for that trait, and only while the Aniimo is assigned there.
  • Personality is a bonus layer, not a key, a Psyche Fruit reroll changes personality (and therefore which facilities get the +20%) but does not change an Aniimo's Home Abilities. (DTGRE)
  • Combat first or homeland first? A battle Aniimo and a worker Aniimo want different letters, that's exactly what Psyche Fruit rerolls are for (§2). Just remember: starters Helion and Lunara can't reroll at all.
  • Facility names are as printed in the in-game Home Bonus panel (via GameWith, Game8 and AniimoTools), if a facility label differs in your game version, the in-game panel wins.

Staffing is only half the homeland. The other half is what you plant. AniimoTools ranks every harvest by Home Coin per plot per hour, sold at the Co-op Store. For tree crops the figure includes the Wood Blocks the tree gives on top of the harvest, and the top of the table is all 40-minute cycles:

🌡️ Climate buildings: temperature zones, honestly labelled

  • Environment buildings set the climate. AniimoTools groups the Cooling Unit, Heat Furnace and Sunlamp as environment facilities: they set your Home's climate (heat, cold, light) that some crops and Aniimo need. The temperature bands are Scorching, Warm, Adequate, Cool and Freeze. (AniimoTools)
  • Wrong temperature means slower growth. A crop planted outside its preferred temperature still grows, it just takes longer. (Steam Community RV / Homeland guide, single community source)
  • Overlapping zones combine. The same community guide works through the maths: a plant sitting in both a Scorching zone and a Cool zone counts itself as Warm, and one in both a Freezing and a Warm zone counts as Cool. Two climate buildings can therefore give you three usable temperature bands at once. single source
  • unverified The "9×9 coverage" figure. A 9×9 tile coverage area for climate buildings is quoted in fan discussions, but it does not appear in AniimoTools' homeland data or the other sources used for this guide, so it is not printed here as fact. Check the building's own range preview when you place it in game; that preview is the final word.

🧂 The Sea Salt bottleneck

Sea Salt is made at the Tidewhisper Sandcastle (the "Quick Recipe: Sea Salt" run) and a long list of cooked dishes asks for it, while only that one facility produces it. A community homeland guide says it flatly: "Salt's the bottleneck here." single community source The practical takeaway, whatever your layout: if a recipe chain stalls, check your salt supply first, and consider running the Sandcastle on salt full-time when you're cooking in bulk.

Steam Community, RV / Homeland Guide · facility data: AniimoTools

🚐 RV Levels 1 to 20: what each upgrade asks for

Your RV level is your Homeland level. It sets how many Aniimo you can place, which facilities and modules you can buy, and how high they can go. This ladder lists, for every level, the cost to reach it, what has to be in place first, and the headline unlock plus reward you get on arrival. F means Farmland plots placed, W means Woodland plots, M means Mines, and Hab means Habitability. Every level from RV 2 on also raises your functional facility cap and adds new stock to the Home Shop and Furniture Store, so those two lines are not repeated in every row.

🔍 How this ladder was verified

Costs, Aniimo caps, build times and prerequisites were taken level by level from AniimoTools, RV Levels and then cross-checked against MetaBot.GG's Homeland guide, which reads the same retail game files. The two agree on the Home Coin ladder, and the numbers add up: RV 2 to RV 20 costs 74,142,140 Home Coin in total, with about 90 hours of build timers if you ran them back to back. The material totals for RV 7 to RV 20 also match when you sum AniimoTools row by row (for example Rough Lumber 4,910 and Coarse-Sifted Ore 4,200 across RV 7 to 10).

Two honest flags. First, the Wood Block and Mineral Sand costs for RV 2 to RV 6 are listed by AniimoTools only: MetaBot notes its file read does not resolve those early material costs, so treat that part as single source. Second, some older summaries list lower Habitability gates (8,000 at RV 10, for example) and a 40 worker cap at RV 20. The retail file sources used here agree on the higher figures printed below (13,000 at RV 10, 45 Aniimo at RV 20), so the older numbers are not used. If your in-game RV screen ever shows a different number, the screen wins.

Module timing flag (added in the 28 October 2026 re-check): the Ecological and Resource Detector unlocks in this ladder follow the module-ladder data published by AniimoTools and Aniiland: the Ecological Module tops out at Lv. 8 (Lv. 7 at RV 17, Lv. 8 at RV 18), and the Resource Detector reaches Lv. 6 at RV 15 on its way to Lv. 8 at RV 19. The game's own RV upgrade text prints those two ladders one step earlier and even promises an Ecological Module Lv. 9, but no Lv. 9 exists in the ladder data, so it is not listed here. The ladder timing is also the one a real game backs up: a player's own Resource Detector already sat at Lv. 5 by RV 14, which only the ladder version allows. Kitchen and Crafting Module timings are agreed by every source that publishes them.

✅ Facility caps re-checked, 28 October 2026

The "Must be in place first" column above lists what an upgrade requires, not how many of a facility you may place. For the placement caps themselves, a fresh audit found Aniiland and AniimoTools in agreement on every facility's maximum count and maximum level at every RV level, and a player's own game confirms the anchors: the Carousel Mill caps at 2 placed, with Lv. 5 unlocking at RV 16 and Lv. 6 at RV 18 (so Lv. 4 is the top at RV 15), and the Well allows 3 placed by RV 14–15 at max Lv. 4, with Lv. 5 not arriving until RV 17. Where a step-up falls between the checkpoints the two sources were compared at, its exact RV rests on Aniiland alone, and the audit says so rather than smoothing it over.

🛠️ Planning tips from the ladder itself

Plots are the hidden gate, not coins, early on. Farmland climbs by 2 every level (4 at RV 2 to 40 at RV 20) and Woodland by 1, so place the next level's plots while the current upgrade timer is still running and they will already be working when it finishes. (MetaBot.GG)

Materials change tier every few levels. RV 2 to 6 ask for Wood Block and Mineral Sand, RV 7 to 10 for Rough Lumber and Coarse-Sifted Ore, RV 11 to 14 for Standard Planks and Sintered Ore Brick, RV 15 to 18 for Laminated Beams and Refined Ore, and RV 19 to 20 for Densified Timber Component and Microcrystalline Ore Plate. Each higher tier is made from the one below at the Woodworking Bench and the Chimney Kiln, so keeping those two facilities running and stockpiling from around RV 5 saves a painful wait later. (AniimoTools · MetaBot.GG)

Titles and Habitability are named as gates, not explained as systems. Student III gates RV 7 and Wayfarer I, II and III gate RV 11, 15 and 19, and Habitability gates every level from RV 10 on. The file sources name those conditions but do not say how you earn the titles or raise Habitability, so this guide does not invent a method for them. Check the title and Habitability panels in game for the current requirements.

🏕️ RV Parks & Aniimo Trips

Your RV does not have to sit at home. Breezy Plains has four public RV Parks, and you can also found a private park of your own. Parks heal your Aniimo, hand out elemental buffs, and, from RV level 6, send Aniimo on trips for regional specialties and Held Items. Everything in this section comes from aniimo.guide's RV Parks page, which is built directly on the game's own in-game help centre (1.0 client), cross-checked against AniimoTools' Homeland pages.

🌼 The Four Public Parks

RV ParkWhere (per the game)Park Manager
Sea of FlowersBetween the Sea of Flowers and a pine forestBen
Nimbus FieldsBetween Nimbus Fields and the MistwoodsUmi
Echoback LandingOn an island beach in Echoback LandingSesa
Driftwise MeadowBy a lake in Driftwise MeadowYu
  • Activate a park by talking to its Park Manager. Until then, the game points you to them. From the Homeland menu you can quickly return to your park, and switch which park you use; public parks themselves are fixed places, you change parks, you do not move them.
  • Parks heal: your Aniimo's HP restores continuously while you are at a park. It works as an alternative to Healer Kim at the Outpost and to Bonfires.
  • Your platform is yours to decorate: Park Board, then Decorate Platform, then drag furniture into place. Other Pathfinders can leave a like on your Park Board.

✨ Park Buffs: Element Essence

How the buff works from the in-game help

Element Essence on a platform = +2% attack and resistance for that element · a "pure" essence = +5%
  • Place an Element Essence on the small platform next to a parking spot. It covers all nine elements (Fire, Water, Grass, Earth, Lightning, Ice, Wind, Dark, Light), one element per essence.
  • To receive the buff, rest for a while in a ride placed at the park, or interact with the terrace seat.
  • You do not need your own essence. Resting at a neighbor's platform that has one gives you exactly the same buff. The game says so itself, so a generous neighbor is a free +2% (or +5%).
  • Item descriptions mention an exchange involving Element Gem ×10 (Pure Element Gem ×10 for pure versions), but the text does not say which way the exchange goes, so this guide does not guess.

aniimo.guide, RV Parks: Park Buffs, your platform and Aniimo trips

🔒 Private RV Parks

Creating one

  • You create a private park at a chosen location, through a Park Manager, for a fee shown when you create it. Creating one makes you leave your current park.
  • The park stays available and you can invite friends; accepting an invitation teleports them there.
  • Stranger access: turn it on and your park enters the random pool. Non-invited Pathfinders assigned to it are reassigned after 7 days.

Moving, leaving, and the ownership question

  • Relocating moves everyone: when a private park relocates, all members move together to the new location. Nobody gets stranded.
  • Removing a player, leaving, or disbanding: those affected are randomly assigned to a public RV Park in the same area. Disbanding refunds 60% of the creation fee.
  • Changing owners: there is no transfer option. The documented creator powers are invite, stranger access, relocate, remove a player, and disband; transferring ownership is not among them, and members get no management powers in the rules (their only documented move is leaving). So relocating is effectively the creator's job, and the only "new owner" route is disband, recreate, and re-invite. (Read from the help-centre rules as listed; the game never prints the words "only the owner can relocate," but every management action in the system belongs to the creator.)

🧭 Aniimo on a Trip: the Signal Transmitter

Trips run through the RV's Signal Transmitter module. Open Aniimo on a Trip (also reachable from the park's Park Board), tap the plus sign, pick an Aniimo, confirm, then tap again and hit GO.

Signal TransmitterRV level neededEffect
Level 16Aniimo Dispatch: the park holds 1 Aniimo
Level 211The park holds 2 Aniimo; unlocks Dispatch · Adventure
Level 316The park holds 3 Aniimo; unlocks Dispatch · Camping
  • Rewards scale in three tiers: a small, moderate, or large amount of regional specialties, plus Held Items of up to Rare, Epic, or Legendary quality. Some materials exist in only one region, and their descriptions tell you to send Aniimo to gather them near that area's RV Park. (aniimo.guide · AniimoTools)
  • Trip lengths (single detailed source, GameWith's RV guide): On Foot 6h, Adventure 12h, Camping 20h, with only On Foot open at first in their playthrough.
  • ⚠️ Early recall loses everything. Recalling Aniimo on a trip forfeits all of that trip's rewards.
  • ⚠️ Travelers are benched: Aniimo placed at the park cannot join combat or exploration parties, and one out on a trip cannot be switched. Do not send a core team member you will miss.
7

🤝 Team Building & Quick Reference

Everything above, condensed into the rules worth memorizing, plus the questions the whole community is still arguing about, marked as open rather than papered over.

🧩 Building a team: what the sources actually support

  • Cover the jobs, not the labels: damage (DPS), gauge-breaking (BREAK), energy (REGEN), sustain (Heal/Support). The role system has no Tank badge, but in Team Combat, the Breaker is the only role that can Tank. (AniimoTools)
  • Your on-field Aniimo's REGEN runs the team's skill economy, only the on-field Aniimo's REGEN counts toward the shared party Energy pool, so who's standing on the field matters. (AniimoTools)
  • Healers are precious: only five exist in the launch build (Skippy, Pranky, Glacy, Flutternym, Gracewing, all Water or Wind). If you catch one, it's worth building. (MetaBot · AniimoGuide)
  • Feed the thumbs-ups: whatever the team, Potential points go to each Aniimo's two Recommended Attributes first, leftovers to HP (it guards against every damage type; P.DEF and M.DEF each cover only one). (AllThings)
  • Personality is the last 4%, not the first: settle stats and skills first, then reroll personality with Psyche Fruit if you want the matching bonus, and never reroll a starter, because you can't.

📊 How one database weights the roles

MetaBot.GG's tier-list ranking algorithm (one site's scoring method, not a game rule) is still a useful sanity check on what each role is "for":

  • DPS: ATK 40% · skill damage 30% · ultimate 30%
  • Breaker: BREAK 45% · BREAK damage 35% · ATK 20%
  • Support: team effects 35% · REGEN 25% · HP 20% · DEF 20%
  • Healer: team effects 35% · HP 25% · DEF 20% · REGEN 20%
  • Regen: REGEN 40% · team effects 30% · HP 15% · DEF 15%

MetaBot.GG methodology. Note it's the only place ATK shows up for Breakers at all, and it's an algorithm weight, not build advice.

🎓 A Worked Example Team: the rules above, applied

Principles are easier to copy from a finished example. This team is built using only facts verified in §1 to §3: every Aniimo named here appears in those sections with the build shown. Treat it as a template, keep the four jobs, and swap in your own Aniimo as you catch them.

SlotAniimoBuild (from §1 and §3)Why it is here
DPS Lunara Stats: ATK first, REGEN second (its own Recommended Attributes). Personality: ISTJ, and Lunara is a locked starter, so no rerolling is needed or possible. The damage dealer. Its panel already wears the flagship DPS pairing (ATK + REGEN), so Potential goes straight into the thumbs-ups.
BREAK Blazen Stats: BREAK, then HP, then the defense matching the fight. Skip ATK entirely. Personality: ISTP (GameWith's pick, §3). The frontline and, in Team Combat, your Tank; Breakers are the only role that can Tank. Blazen is the Breaker AniimoTools actually measured: at 510 ATK versus 0.85 × 770 BREAK = 654, it swung entirely on BREAK.
REGEN Leafy Stats: REGEN first (its signature skill grows with REGEN, cap 500), HP second. Personality: ISTJ. The battery. Only the on-field Aniimo's REGEN feeds the shared party Energy pool, so rotate Leafy in whenever the team's skills need refilling.
HEAL Gracewing Stats: HP first (its heals are a share of its own Max HP), REGEN second. Personality: ISTJ (AllThings' build). The sustain. Its team heal restores 30% of its Max HP to everyone at once, plus 9% over 8 seconds, so every HP point you give it is healing for the whole team.
  • How the fight flows: Blazen opens and drains the guard gauge; Lunara spends the opening hitting into it; Leafy rotates in to keep Energy flowing for everyone's skills; Gracewing tops the team up between waves.
  • What to upgrade first: thumbs-up stats on all four, in team order. Personality rerolls come last (and never for Lunara).
  • No Gracewing yet? Any of the other four playable healers (Skippy, Pranky, Glacy, Flutternym) fills the slot with the same HP-first build. Healers are rare enough that the first one you catch is the right one to build.

❔ Still genuinely open, nobody has the answer yet

  • Role headcounts (other than Heal): four sources count four ways and none reconcile, see the table in §1.
  • A full 1-to-6 stat order per role: no source publishes one. The longest real chains cover 3–4 stats; anything longer would be inference, so this guide doesn't print one.
  • Breaker personalities, settled by testing: the ESTP-vs-ISTP argument (§3) is argued from mechanism on both sides, nobody has published comparative testing.
  • Support basics, final word: floor vs flat 10.5 × level (§1), the floor reading is better supported and claims developer confirmation, but there's no third independent source.
  • Held-item specifics: item count (24 vs 25), per-item effects, rarity enhancement caps and reset costs remain unverified, see the quarantine box in §4. (Two conditions were verified on 28 Oct 2026 and moved into §4: +2 Potential at enhancement +10, and the Legendary Lv 15 Tier 2 effect and Contract.)
  • An official word: no official Pawprint Studio page, patch note or post stating personality bonuses, stat priorities or role counts was found, everything here comes from guide and database sites, several working directly from the in-game help and panels.

8

🔍 Myth-Busting FAQ

The traps this guide's research kept running into, gathered in one place. Every verdict below points back to the section where it was checked; nothing here is a new claim, just the greatest hits of wrong.

"ATK helps my Breaker hit harder." busted

For 25 of the 26 Breakers, it does not. A Breaker's basic attacks run on max(ATK, 0.85 × BREAK), and nearly every Breaker's BREAK side wins, so ATK points sit there doing nothing. Popota is the lone exception. Feed BREAK, HP, and the defense that matches the fight instead. (§1)

"BREAK adds damage for my DPS." busted

BREAK Potential on a DPS drains the enemy's guard gauge faster, and that is all it does. It never adds HP damage. The flagship DPS panels in game wear ATK + REGEN for a reason. (§1)

"REGEN means my Aniimo heals itself / moves faster." busted

REGEN is Energy recovery speed: how fast skills come back. It is not HP regeneration and it is not a Speed stat. And only the on-field Aniimo's REGEN feeds the shared party Energy pool. (§1)

"Personality can change as they level up." busted

It cannot. Personality is rolled when the Aniimo is obtained or hatched, and levels and evolution never touch it. The only way it ever changes is a Psyche Fruit, and even that is a full random reroll of all four letters. Starters Helion and Lunara cannot change at all. (§2)

"Traits come in strengths: Somewhat, Relatively, Very." busted

That ladder exists in the game's data files, but AniimoTools, which found it there, states it does nothing: no effect attached, and no Aniimo can ever be given one. In the live game every letter is worth one fixed bonus. (§2)

"A Psyche Fruit lets me pick the personality I want." busted

It rerolls all four letters at random, with no confirmation pop-up before the change lands. Landing one exact code can take several fruit at 100 Glimmer each, so budget for rerolls, not for a menu. (§2)

"That colored grade badge is a paw print." busted

It is a face. The Potential grade badges (green Common, blue Good, purple Elite, gold Perfect) are little colored faces, and the Perfect one even smiles. When both Recommended Attributes roll 10, the Perfect badge puts on sunglasses. (§4)

"I need a Copper Fruit for my Aniimo." wrong name

Some videos call it a Copper Fruit, the item's name is Capafruit: +1 Innate Potential to all six stats, once per Aniimo. It pays off most on an Aniimo whose two Recommended Attributes both sit at Innate 9, crowning both at 10. (§4)

"I can transfer my private RV Park to a friend." busted

There is no ownership transfer in the game's documented rules. The creator's powers are invite, stranger access, relocate, remove a player, and disband, and the park lives with whoever created it. The only handover is disband (60% of the fee back), let the new owner create a fresh park, and re-invite everyone. (§6)
